finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the user-supplied 'target' query parameter straight to http.Get and returns the response body. An attacker can make the server request internal hosts, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), or localhost services, and read the responses.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) (main.go:16), with the response body copied back to the client at main.go:22

trace.note: /fetch is registered to the fetch handler
target is read from the query string with no processing
http.Get(target) makes the outbound request to the attacker-chosen URL
The response body is returned to the attacker (full-read SSRF). Errors are also echoed at line 18.

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, or IP validation, no allowlist, and no authentication on the path. The default http.Client follows redirects and has no custom dialer that blocks private IPs. I checked safeFetch (main.go:25) and did not report it. It requires the hostname to be in the allowlist (main.go:27) and fetches the re-serialized URL, so the only residual risk is an allowlisted host issuing an open redirect.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the query param 'target' directly to http.Get with no validation, middleware, or auth (handler registered at main.go:41), and main.go:22 copies the response body back to the client; the allowlist at main.go:27 applies only to /safe.
